snippet.title: Amiga 500 Longplay [083] The Quest for the Time Bird
snippet.description:
http://www.longplays.org

Played by: Ironclaw

Subscribe: http://tinyurl.com/iamironclawsub

Released in 1989 and based on the French comic (since 1983) 'La quÃªte de l'oiseau du temps'.

The introduction part from the manual:

****************************************************************
Based on the graphic novel of the same name, this computer game THE QUEST FOR THE TIME-BIRD is a marvelous saga whose principal ingredients are action, danger, suspense, fantasy and magic.

In an unknown world, at a time when wizards and witches cast their magic spells, you play a series of roles:

ROXANNA: Daughter of Mara the Witch (and perhaps of Bragon the Knight). Her mother has given her the task of completing the quest. Her weapon is a scorching whip, woven from the hide of a Borak slain by Bragon.

BRAGON THE KNIGHT: This most valorous and experienced of all knights has been living quietly on his estate for many years. Only the arrival of Roxanna and an interest in the Quest can persuade him to return to a life of danger and mortal combat. With him goes his trusty war-axe, the Reaper.

Roxanna and Bragon will become acquainted with Bulrog and the Unknown knight. They may very well accompany you if you wish it.

In the farm-house, Mara explains your task to you. Listen well, for each detail has its importance.

9 days remain for you to complete the Quest.
****************************************************************

There will be a couple of disk messages in this video, which I usually get rid of, but couldn't this time as it had music playing during the message. I tried to insert the required disk right before it was required, but wouldn't work as it first wanted to check the previous disk before having the other one inserted. I know this can be avoided with WHDLoad, but I only use that when I really need to as it tens to crash often with save states.

The game ran much smoother on a faster Amiga, like the A1200, but had sound/animation/sync issues in a few places then, so ran it with normal A500 speed. So, with A500, it doesn't load as fast as it would with A1200 (but still fast enough for me not to bother editing out any loading), the map traveling is not as smooth and fast, and the lightning at the end where I added the game over part doesn't flash fast enough to look as good as it did on the A1200.

At 16:11, the text starting with "But before" only lasted for about 1 frame for some reason, tried it many times, so to make it stay for at least a few seconds I slowed the Amiga down a bit. Pause if you need to. I think the problem might be because the last panel is located ON the same plane as the exit, so it triggers exit at the same time. Couldn't find an area that only had the panel.

18:40, now a blue dot appeared, and if I go there, the game is complete. But, before I finish the game, I wanted to show the land mounts first and some other people + eating food and resting. so I went to Thousand Greens first. After that, on my way to the blue dot, I decided to show each character's attack, as we've only seen the archer dude up to now, so I traveled around a bit first.

There were more places to visit and people/creatures to encounter, like the creature called MORG in the White March. He was annoying, kept following me around, wanted to play games. He looks like some sort of big worm/walrus type of thing, and he wears a monocle. Like I said, more places and stuff to see, but I settled with what I recorded. Could also buy weapons and stuff.

I found 2 walkthroughs, both calling the "Desert" area the "Sand Lips". Guess there are other versions of the game? Or maybe they played with French/German language and their translation is "Sand Lips"? Maybe that's what the place is called in the French comics. The game can be completed in different ways. My first attempt using one of the walkthroughs was very different to the one I went with, and had me first travel to the Thousand Greens and recruit someone there. Had to go with another walkthrough (by Drudkh over at EACool as I got stuck.

One of the things I can encounter while traveling is an old lady who wants to take a look in my bag(s). I get 3 options of answers when the dialogue opens up, but doesn't matter which one I pick, she will steal something from me (which is not obvious if you don't check afterwards), so I had to kill her.

I need to land on the dot to enter the area in all places except the one at the very top of the map (Ridj), as I couldn't move that far up to reach it, but in this case the game was OK with just being close enough.

14:52, I know she wants one of the men to talk to her, but wanted to speak to her with Rox first so you know what she's after Smile

22:22, sometimes they are too eager to kill something or just continue, so even though I selected the guy, I didn't even get to select the target before Rox took actions into her own hands. -
